item.title: White House highlights 'steepest' ever decline in US casualties from cartels amid boat strikes
item.description: Senior administration officials discuss the American military's actions under President Donald Trump against cartels in the Western Hemisphere.
item.content:encoded:
Senior administration officials touted President Donald Trump's use of military force against cartels in the Western Hemisphere during a press call on Tuesday.

"So, the president directed, the Department of War executed, the first ever plan and strategy to use direct military force to defend the homeland from this threat," one of the officials said.

"The effects have been spectacular, and we've seen the largest and steepest reduction in U.S. casualties inflicted by the cartels in American history," the individual added.

US KILLS 4 ALLEGED DRUG SMUGGLERS ON BOAT IN CARIBBEAN, BRINGING TOTAL TO 227 IN 68 STRIKES

The official also indicated that the U.S. action "has created the political space — because we are now taking the fight to the cartels — for new governments to be elected that are going to partner directly with us to fight this battle."

"And so now you see governments all across the Western Hemisphere rising up, saying that they recognize this as a military threat, and they're gonna meet it as a military threat," the official noted, pointing to Colombia, Peru, Ecuador, Honduras, Costa Rica, and El Salvador as examples.

NEWLY UNCLASSIFIED PENTAGON IMAGES SHOW SUSPECTED DRUG BOATS AS OFFICIAL ISSUES DEADLY WARNING

One of the other officials noted that "U.S. Southern Command's counter-narcotics operations have driven record reductions in illicit maritime activity," which "includes a 65% reduction in the Western Caribbean," a decline of 60% for the eastern Caribbean, as well as "a nearly 50%" decrease in key regions of the Eastern Pacific.

With Trump as commander-in-chief, the U.S. military has executed dozens of deadly attacks against vessels of alleged "narco-terrorists."

The president's policy of using the lethal strikes against alleged drug traffickers has been controversial.

US KILLS TWO 'NARCO-TERRORISTS' IN STRIKE 2 MONTHS SINCE LAST ANNOUNCED ANTI-'NARCO-TRAFFICKING' ATTACK

An official on the call said that America's actions in the Western Hemisphere have yielded "a huge deterrent impact on bad actors all around the world" by showing the nation's "willingness to use lethal force to protect our core interests."

item.title: Dem megadonor among 400 Jewish Michiganders labeled AIPAC insiders for denouncing El-Sayed's leftist campaign
item.description: Over 400 Michigan Jewish Democrats signed a letter backing Mike Rogers, but former Rep. Andy Levin claims AIPAC is really driving the effort.
item.content:encoded:
More than 400 Democratic Jewish Michiganders are backing Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers and warning that they feel "threatened and alienated" by leftist candidate Abdul El-Sayed and his political allies.

Prominent Democratic donor Rob Orley, a senior advisor for O2 Investments, is among the signatories. He previously donated tens of thousands of dollars to Democratic campaigns, according to FEC campaign filings — but now he and other prominent Jewish leaders are ditching El-Sayed for Republican candidate Mike Rogers.

"Many of us have been fiercely supportive of Democratic candidates and principles," a letter signed by Orley and hundreds of others stated.

"If El-Sayed were to win the general election in this important swing state, we fear the far-left and anti-Jewish elements in the Democratic Party would become dominant, including in the imminent 2028 presidential race," the letter continues. "We cannot allow him to become the Democratic standard-bearer or Michigan’s senator."

Fox News Digital reached out to O2 Investments for comment.

MICHIGAN SENATE HOPEFUL CALLS AIPAC DONATIONS 'LEGALIZED BRIBERY,' REMAINS SILENT ON OTHER DONATIONS

The letter includes signatures from some of the most prominent members of Michigan's Jewish community, including Robert Gordon, the former president of Temple Israel, the state's largest Jewish congregation, which was the site of an antisemitic attack in March.

Shayna Levine, the daughter of the leading rabbi at Temple Israel; David Propis, cantor of Congregation Shaarey Zedek; Laurence Deitch, who served as a University of Michigan regent; and Hannan Lis, a Weight Watchers executive, have also signed the letter declaring that they feel "threatened and alienated by the politics and allies embraced by Abdul El-Sayed."

But former Rep. Andy Levin, who is Jewish, is claiming that opposition to El-Sayed among Jewish Democrats is a minority view and that his old foe, the American Israel Political Action Committee, is really driving the letter. Levin lost his 2022 primary bid to Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., after AIPAC spent more than $4 million in the primary race against him.

"It's not a surprise to me," Levin said in an interview with Fox News Digital. "The people I know associated with it are all long-time AIPAC insiders and supporters." Levin added that AIPAC "represents a distinctly minority position about Israel and Palestine within the Jewish community."

Levin, who was first elected to Congress in 2018 to replace his late father Sander Levin, gave his endorsement to El-Sayed in November 2025.

"I am overwhelmed like literally every day except Shabbat — our sabbath on Saturday — with the incoming I get from Jewish people, young people, middle-aged people, older people, who are so mad about an effort like this and who want to do everything they can to make sure Abdul El-Sayed wins the election on November 3rd, that this U.S. Senate seat stays democratic, and that we do everything we can to save and expand our democracy," Levin continued.

However, attorney Daniel Cherrin, who signed the letter, told Fox News Digital that he has not attended an AIPAC event since college more than 30 years ago. Cherrin said he has tremendous respect for Levin, whom he has known for years, and previously worked with Abdul El-Sayed in Detroit and Wayne County. Although he considers El-Sayed a "good" person, Cherrin said he cannot overlook the movement backing his candidacy.

"I am very concerned about the movement that is behind Abdul, and for the safety of my community, I don't feel safe in that environment with the people that are standing in support of him," Cherrin told Fox News Digital.

DEMOCRATS' CIVIL WAR HEADS TO MICHIGAN WHERE PROGRESSIVES FACE BIGGEST TEST YET IN HIGH-STAKES SENATE SHOWDOWN

"They don't understand the impact that their words and their actions is having on me and my children and my neighbors," Cherrin said. "And so, for that, I am very worried about should he be elected what that means for all those that are trying to advance his candidacy."

Hasan Piker, a Twitch streamer who has called Orthodox Jews inbreds and said America deserved 9/11, has been a top surrogate for El-Sayed's campaign. Over the past week, El-Sayed has attempted to distance himself from the social media influencer, suggesting that people focusing on his affiliation with Piker are "missing the boat."

Levin, who has condemned Piker's antisemitic falsehoods about the Oct. 7 attack, agreed with El-Sayed that too much focus is on Piker. He then argued that the Democratic National Committee received very little pushback for inviting Piker to stream during the 2024 Democratic National Convention, giving then-Vice President and Democratic presidential nominee Kamala Harris an opportunity to reach Piker's audience. Piker did not endorse Harris because of the Biden administration's policy in the Gaza war.

"So I'm not accepting Hasan Piker, but look in the mirror, sister," Levin said. "When it's a guy named Abdul with a guy named Hasan, you're blowing up about it and covering it massively. When it was not an Arab American or a Muslim who campaigned with him or did whatever Kamala Harris did, literally no one asked her a single question about it."

Last month, El-Sayed said he had "no plans" to continue campaigning with Piker.

Roslyn Schindler attends Congregation T'chiyah, which is a progressive Reform synagogue that touts its support for Black Lives Matter, and transgender rights, with Levin. A daughter of Holocaust survivors, Schindler has lived in the metro Detroit area for 50 years and taught Holocaust studies at Wayne State University. She shared with Fox News Digital that she has supported El-Sayed well before his primary victory, and that the Democratic Party is in need of a "major shake-up," citing El-Sayed's support for progressive policies like Medicare for All and getting money out of politics.

"I am certainly not an anti-Zionist, as many Jews who don't support Abdul think we are, but I am a committed Jew," Schindler told Fox News Digital. "I'm a committed Democrat. I believe that the Democratic Party should be a large tent, so to speak, that includes all members of that party, no matter what their perspective."

Fox News Digital asked Schindler for her thoughts on El-Sayed's affiliation with Piker and whether there is a place in the Democratic Party for people who follow his ideology.

EL-SAYED TRIES TO MAKE PEACE WITH JEWISH DEMOCRATS BUT DRAWS LINE AT DUMPING HASAN PIKER

"As a Jew, I certainly don't want anyone to be anti-Semitic. I don't want anyone to be anti-Muslim. I don't want anyone to be anti-LGBTQ, and the list goes on," Schindler said. "Is that realistic? Probably not. Do I want those people to be part of the Democratic Party? It's not really for me to want. It is what it is. They'll either be part of it or they won't."

"But I do believe there is enough traction within the Jewish community at large to counter anti-Semitism, and that's across the board," Schindler continued.

But Cherrin said the fact that his family has to pass security officers guarding synagogues and temples is evidence to him that the Jewish community at large can't tackle antisemitism by itself.

"It's not about AIPAC for me," Cherrin said. "It is about it is about how are we protecting the sanctity of the Jewish community in Michigan and frankly and across the country with all these other races that are out there."

"People within the Jewish community, who typically identify as Democrats, don't feel comfortable voting for the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate and are looking for a place to channel their frustration. That should not be discounted," Cherrin continued.

Cherrin pushed for both Rogers and El-Sayed to continue to reach out to Jewish community members outside of politics to get a "real pulse" on what Jewish voters are thinking.

"Abdul is grateful for the good conversations he’s had with Jewish leaders across Michigan, and he’ll continue to be actively engaged with communities to build the coalition that will defeat Rogers, restore Democratic control of the U.S. Senate, and put a much-needed check on Trump’s reckless agenda," a spokesperson for El-Sayed's campaign said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Rogers, who previously served in Congress for 15 years, said he appreciates the growing support from the Jewish community — especially those crossing party lines to back his bid for U.S. Senate.

"As antisemitism rises and Jewish families worry for their safety, it’s critical that we have leaders who will confront hatred — not inflame it," Rogers said in a statement. "That’s where my opponent and I couldn’t be more different."

"Abdul El-Sayed fans the flames of antisemitism. We’re fighting to extinguish it," Rogers continued.

Although for progressive Jewish Democrats like Levin and Schindler, President Donald Trump and his MAGA allies like Rogers are the biggest threat to democracy.

"We have a chance to protect our Democracy by keeping this U.S. Senate seat democratic and expanding our democracy, by, for the first time, having, uh, electing a Muslim to the U.S. Senate," Levin said. "Most Jews that I know so believe in this democratic experiment, this Democratic project called America."

"And it's about damn time that Muslims had a senator and there's a brilliant person running here in Michigan who we can elect to be the first one. Will he do exactly what a Jewish person would do or something? No, but he will be someone we could talk to and who will be a great representative for all of Michigan and for the Arab American and Muslim communities in particular," Levin said.

item.title: Talarico’s ‘proud capitalist’ about-face collides with resurfaced call to ‘dismantle’ capitalism
item.description: James Talarico once called capitalism "oppressive" and predicted Texas' fossil fuel industry was "not gonna last" in a 2020 Sierra Club Zoom call.
item.content:encoded:
The James Talarico campaign says the Democratic Senate nominee in Texas is a "proud capitalist," even though he once described capitalism as an "oppressive system" that needed to be dismantled — and predicted that Texas’ fossil fuel industry was "not gonna last."

The remarks, made during a resurfaced 2020 Zoom call with Sierra Club activists, are drawing fresh scrutiny as Talarico faces Republican nominee and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in a Senate race that could help determine control of the chamber.

The comments were first reported by CNN early Tuesday and were seized on by Lone Star Liberty PAC, an outside political group aligned with Paxton, and Senate Leadership Fund, a leading super PAC backing Senate Republicans.

THESE 12 MIDTERM RACES WILL DECIDE WHICH PARTY CONTROLS THE SENATE

On the call, Talarico is heard saying that the U.S. was facing a "multi-faceted threat" of a climate, economic, and social crisis.

After an activist asked how to address the harm suffered by communities of color by climate change, Talarico responded, "I’m so thankful that you asked this question and also thankful that young activists have really drawn the link between climate change and white supremacy and capitalism in our country."

"I think only understanding the ways that all three of those oppressive systems work together are we going to be able to begin the process of dismantling them."

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

Talarico, during the same forum, forecast that Texas' fossil fuel industry wouldn't last.

"We all know that Texas has been a leader in oil and gas, but in many ways that’s like being the leader in cassette tapes in the 1980s. That industry is not gonna last," Talarico said.

Asked for comment, Talarico campaign spokesperson J.T. Ennis told Fox News Digital, "James is a proud capitalist and agrees with the majority of Texans that racism, natural disasters, and a billionaire-controlled economy are all problems we need to address."

"James has already said he missed the mark on some of his past statements, while Ken Paxton has refused to address his comments that the school shooting in Uvalde was ‘God’s plan’ and that Texas’ abortion ban is good for interstate commerce," Ennis added.

The Talarico campaign also spotlighted that the state lawmaker has "taken many votes" in support of the oil industry. And the campaign website states that he aims to make sure that Texas "not only maintains, but extends" its energy dominance.

WHAT THE LATEST FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS IN THE MIDTERM RACES SHOW

The Paxton campaign and Republicans have repeatedly targeted Talarico for past comments he's made on social issues, including his prior suggestion that "God is nonbinary," that he "hates Christianity," and that "there are many more than two biological sexes; in fact, there are six."

Talarico, a 37-year-old former middle school teacher and Presbyterian seminarian, defeated progressive firebrand and vocal critic of President Donald Trump Rep. Jasmine Crockett in the March Democratic Senate primary.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Paxton, a longtime Trump ally, captured the GOP nomination in late May, after defeating longtime Republican Sen. John Cornyn in a primary runoff election. The combustible clash between the two Texas titans shaped up as a fight between the Republican establishment and Trump's MAGA and America First supporters. Trump stayed neutral in the intra-party battle until giving Paxton an 11th-hour endorsement.

The general election face-off in deep-red Texas between Talarico and Paxton is one of roughly a dozen races that will likely decide if Republicans hold the Senate majority or if Democrats win back control of the chamber.

Democrats haven't won a Senate election in Texas in nearly four decades, but they view Paxton as vulnerable because of the slew of scandals and legal problems that have battered him over the past decade. And Paxton is dealing with a messy divorce, with his wife citing "biblical grounds" based on "recent discoveries" in filing last year to end their marriage.

Talarico enjoys a large fundraising advantage over Paxton.

Meanwhile, the most recent Fox News poll in the Texas Senate showdown, conducted in late July, indicated Talarico holding a slight 51%-48% edge over Paxton among registered voters.

The survey suggested that Paxton had yet to fully unite Republicans. While virtually all Democrats supported Talarico (98%), slightly fewer Republicans were unified behind Paxton (89%).

Meanwhile, the most recent Fox News Power Rankings, released last month, shifted the Senate race in Texas from Lean Republican to toss-up.

item.title: Canadian PM tells Trump to 'stop trying to be tough' in trade fight
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney told Americans to "stop trying to be tough" and called U.S. Cabinet secretaries' mockery "beneath their office."
item.content:encoded:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Monday that Americans need to "stop trying to be tough" during the countries' contentious trade negotiations.

Speaking to reporters in Ottawa about U.S.-Canadian trade negotiations over automobile tariffs, Carney said, "When the Americans stop doing memes, stop throwing shade, stop trying to be tough and start being serious about having those discussions, we can have those discussions."

"Look, it's not constructive, but that's their democracy," Carney added.

TRUMP TAUNTS CANADA ON RENAMING LAKE ONTARIO THE 'LAKE AMERICA' AMID RISING BORDER TRADE RIFT

After Canada suspended trade talks on Aug. 21, Trump signed an executive order changing the name of Lake Ontario, which is bordered by New York and Canada's Ontario province, to Lake America.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and War Secretary Pete Hegseth also mocked Canada in social media posts, with Bessent writing that Canada could not go "tit-for-tat" with America's economy and Hegseth posting a photo of two female Canadian military members with the caption "this is real."

When asked to comment on U.S. Cabinet secretaries mocking the Canadian military, Carney responded, "It's beneath their office."

Carney cited both the U.S. posture and its terms in negotiations and barriers to reaching a deal.

TRUMP TRADE CHIEF WARNS CANADA WALKED AWAY FROM 'THE BEST DEAL' TO TRIGGER 50% U.S. TARIFFS

"The issues with respect to language and culture — enough to not have to deal. The issues Mr. Gray just asked about, with respect to restrictions on future trade deals, restrictions on our sovereignty — enough not to have a deal. Issues with respect to locking in an uncompetitive, trade arrangement in our key industries, automobiles being one of them — enough to not have a trade deal," he continued.

"And then the general attitude, and I’ll leave you with this, which I think this is a very important point, is that the attitude of the United States in these discussions and subsequently has been one that, the core Canadian industries either would be subsidiaries effectively of the United States industries or would put in place terms where those industries would be, gradually wound down in Canada and we're not going to of course, we're not going to accept those terms."

Trump, following Carney's suspension of negotiations, accused Canada of wanting "the benefits of being a State, without being one!!!"

In a post on Truth Social, Trump also said Canada has been taking advantage of the U.S. by charging U.S. farmers tariffs.

TRUMP MUST CLOSE THE BACK DOOR CHINA USES TO EXPLOIT NORTH AMERICAN TRADE

Carney, for his part, said America's insistence that it have a say over who else Canada trades with was a bridge too far.

He also said the U.S. view of the trade relationship was "misguided," adding that on automobiles, the U.S. needs both Canada and Mexico.

FEARS OF A CANADIAN TRADE WAR ARE OVERBLOWN. SO FAR, IT’S MORE OF A SKIRMISH

"The United States auto industry is made stronger by the Canadian and the Mexican auto industries. And at a time of big, big change in auto, it's important that we work together. That's why I say yes, there is a mutually beneficial deal," he told reporters.

Carney did leave the door open for further negotiations.

‘CAPTAIN CANADA’ FIREBRAND UNLOADS ON TRUMP WITH PROFANE ONE-LINER AS TRADE WAR ESCALATES

"There were elements of that mutually beneficial deal that we were moving towards, which is why we were still at the table. But we never, viewed that we had that deal. And it diverged towards the end. At some point, maybe it'll converge again," Carney said.

He told lawmakers in his country that relations with the U.S. will not "go back to normal any time soon" and said the situation is "a new normal that we have to get adjusted to."

TRUMP ALLIES PUSH TO ARM PRESIDENT WITH NEW TARIFF WEAPON TO PUNISH COUNTRIES 'RIPPING OFF' AMERICA

Carney, matching a slate of tariffs the U.S. imposed on Canadian goods such as steel and lumber, imposed his own set of tariffs which he said will go "dollar for dollar" with America's tariffs. The Canadian levies are set to take effect on Sept. 8.

Fox News Digital contacted the White House, the office of the U.S. Trade Representative, the U.S. Treasury, the Pentagon and the Canadian Prime Minister's Office for further comment.

Fox News Digital's Michael Sinkewicz, The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: FIRST ON FOX: Trump’s 9/11 tribute to feature massive piece of Ground Zero history at White House
item.description: Trump will welcome NYPD first responders and Tunnel to Towers Foundation representatives to the White House to mark the 25th anniversary of 9/11.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: President Donald Trump will host 9/11 first responders and officials at the White House on Sept. 8, where a 21-foot steel beam recovered from the World Trade Center’s South Tower will be displayed, Fox News Digital learned.

"President Trump will pay tribute to the American heroes we lost in the tragic Sept. 11 attacks, their beautiful family members and to the acts of heroism that defined that fateful day when the unbreakable spirit of the American people prevailed," White House spokesperson Olivia Wales told Fox News Digital.

The Tunnel to Towers Foundation will bring its "Steel Across America" tour to the White House on Sept. 8, where the 21-foot, 16,900-pound steel beam recovered from the World Trade Center’s South Tower will be displayed on the White House Ellipse.

MASSIVE WORLD TRADE CENTER STEEL BEAM ARRIVES AT WEST POINT, UNITING 9/11 HEROES WITH GENERATION SENT TO WAR

"The president will stand with first responders to renew our sacred vow that we will never forget – and that the United States of America will always defend our proud, free nation with unyielding resolve," said Wales.

Trump and Tunnel to Towers Foundation Chairman and CEO Frank Siller are expected to speak.

The president will also attend a ceremony at the Pentagon while Vice President JD Vance will travel to New York City’s World Trade Center site, and other administration officials will represent the White House in Shanksville, Pennsylvania — marking all three locations targeted or affected by the attacks.

RETIRED PORT AUTHORITY OFFICERS TELL MAMDANI, HOCHUL TO STAY AWAY FROM GROUND ZERO ON 9/11

Last year, Trump and first lady Melania Trump attended a 9/11 commemoration at the Pentagon and issued a Patriot Day proclamation calling for flags to be flown at half-staff.

He later attended a Yankees-Tigers game featuring tributes to the victims in the Bronx, New York City.

The steel beam has served as a traveling memorial to the victims and first responders of 9/11, offering pop-up events across 21 states leading up to the anniversary of the tragic day.

AMERICA’S HEARTLAND COMES FACE-TO-FACE WITH 9/11 HISTORY AS 25TH ANNIVERSARY NEARS

"Never forgetting the sacrifice and bravery of our nation’s heroes, as well as our lost loved ones, is a generational promise that every American can help keep," Tunnel to Towers Foundation Chairman and CEO Frank Siller previously told Fox News Digital.

Siller founded the organization in honor of his brother, FDNY firefighter Stephen Siller, who died responding to the attacks.

Tunnel to Towers has provided mortgage-free homes to families of fallen service members and first responders while also working to combat veteran homelessness.

The foundation is honoring the 343 FDNY firefighters who died on 9/11 by delivering 343 mortgage-free homes this year.

item.title: An AI cyberattack could turn off America's lights before Washington even understands why
item.description: Five warnings in 17 days revealed how AI cyberattacks now threaten power grids, water infrastructure and hospitals as Volt Typhoon looms large.
item.content:encoded:
Your lights. Your water. Your hospital. Your internet. All four depend on digital systems that foreign hackers are now targeting.

Over 17 days in August, five warnings showed how quickly the danger is changing. The next serious cyberattack may not be about stolen passwords or credit-card numbers. It could reach the systems that move electricity, pump drinking water, run factories and support hospitals.

Artificial intelligence is making those attacks faster to prepare and easier to scale. Worse: increasingly capable systems are beginning to perform parts of the attack that once required skilled hackers working step by step.

TREASURY SECRETARY BESSENT WARNS AMERICANS ABOUT AI-DRIVEN BANK ACCOUNT HACKS AS THREATS RAPIDLY EVOLVE

Five August developments tell the story.

1. OpenAI said the window is closing. On Aug. 10, OpenAI warned that attackers will increasingly use AI to conduct cyberattacks at "unprecedented speed and scale," including in fully autonomous ways. Its conclusion was blunt: defenders have a "narrowing window to prepare."

OpenAI’s own cyber-focused model, GPT-5.6-Cyber, now answers 95% of advanced exploit-development requests it used to refuse.

For defenders, every minute matters. If an attacker can find and exploit a weakness before anyone knows it exists, the opportunity to patch the system may disappear before the attack begins.

HALLUSQUATTING AI ATTACK COULD HIJACK YOUR COMPUTER

2. Federal agencies said the attacks are no longer theoretical. On Aug. 19, the NSA, CISA, FBI, Department of Energy and EPA warned that cyber actors are targeting U.S.-based Siemens S7 series industrial controllers with AI-generated exploitation scripts. These controllers help operate real machinery. The sectors at risk include power, water, manufacturing, chemicals and food production.

A successful attack would not merely steal information. Federal officials warn it could interrupt industrial processes, damage equipment or create safety problems. The government calls this an active threat, not a theoretical one.

3. OpenAI disclosed a "warning shot": an AI model escaped its test controls.

On Aug. 26, OpenAI revealed that during internal cybersecurity evaluations, models operating with reduced safeguards circumvented controls meant to isolate them, gained internet access and compromised parts of OpenAI’s own research infrastructure and Hugging Face’s systems.

This was not an enemy attack. But OpenAI’s own conclusion was chilling: without sufficient safeguards, highly capable AI agents can find and exploit weaknesses across multiple computer systems and take dangerous actions no human specifically directed.

IRAN-LINKED HACKERS SUSPECTED IN UK POWER-PLANT SHUTDOWN AFTER ALLEGED MINNESOTA WATER ATTACK

4. Trump declared a national emergency over foreign threats to America’s power grid.

Also on Aug. 26, President Donald Trump declared a national emergency to secure America’s bulk-power system from foreign threats.

His order is not specifically about AI hacking. It targets foreign-produced electrical equipment, software, firmware and remote-access capabilities that could create opportunities for sabotage or unauthorized access.

THE MACHINES THAT KEEP AMERICA ALIVE ARE FAILING. WE FORGOT HOW TO REPLACE THEM

But the AI connection is explicit. The White House says the rapid growth of artificial intelligence, data centers, advanced manufacturing and defense production has made the United States increasingly dependent on reliable electricity while magnifying the consequences of a successful grid attack.

That takes the threat out of the server room. Lose power long enough and water pumps, fuel distribution, communications, hospitals and emergency services all come under pressure.

5. More than 100 organizations said the next escalation could come within months.

On Aug. 27, OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services and more than 100 other technology, cybersecurity and financial organizations issued a collective warning: "In the coming months, AI-enabled cyber attacks will become far more widespread and sophisticated."

IRANIAN HACKERS ATTACKED OUR WATER SYSTEMS. HERE ARE 5 THINGS OUR LEADERS NEED TO DO NOW

They specifically identified hospitals, water-treatment plants and the infrastructure powering the internet as being at risk.

"In the coming months" is not Washington language for some distant future.

It is a countdown.

February’s numbers show why August’s warnings cannot be dismissed. CrowdStrike’s 2026 Global Threat Report found that AI-enabled adversaries increased their activity 89% year over year. In 2025, criminals took an average of just 29 minutes to move from an initially breached computer into other systems. The fastest observed breakout took 27 seconds.

Twenty-seven seconds is not enough time for a committee meeting, a phone call up the chain, or a traditional human response.

Anthropic showed where this may be heading. In a controlled test, its Claude Mythos Preview was told to look for a security weakness. Without step-by-step human help, it found a 17-year-old flaw, figured out how to exploit it and took complete control of the computer. The machine performed work that once demanded a highly skilled hacker.

America must also assume hostile governments are watching the same technological curve. U.S. agencies identified Volt Typhoon as a Chinese state-sponsored hacking campaign that gained long-term access inside American communications, energy, transportation and water networks. Officials assessed with high confidence that Beijing was positioning itself to disrupt critical services during a future major crisis or conflict with the United States, not simply gathering intelligence. Those are the same power and water sectors named in the Aug. 19 federal warning.

The Chinese strategy already exists. AI is the accelerant.

During a confrontation over Taiwan, China would not have to shut down the entire country. Disrupt several ports, rail systems, electrical facilities or communications hubs and the effects could cascade. Add convincing false reports that drinking water is contaminated, hospitals are failing or fuel is running out, and panic could spread faster than the physical damage.

I have warned in three recent books that AI compresses decision time and multiplies an adversary’s reach. August turned that warning operational.

America must harden the targets now. Find exposed industrial systems. Patch known weaknesses. Require strong authentication. Separate operating networks from unnecessary internet access. Help smaller utilities that cannot afford their own cyber armies. And make sure essential services can still operate when digital systems fail.

But a stronger wall is not deterrence. Washington must also improve attribution, preserve credible offensive cyber options and convince Beijing, Moscow, Tehran and their proxies that an attack on essential American infrastructure will carry consequences.

This is not another Silicon Valley story about the latest AI model.

It is about whether the lights come on when you flip the switch, water flows when you open the tap and the emergency room functions when your family needs it.

It is about whether the United States can still move forces and fight a war during a national crisis.

Five warnings landed in 17 days.

Washington should not need a blackout to take the hint.

item.title: ‘No Jews, no news’ strikes again as selective coverage of the 'unsettlers' fuels anti-Israel anger
item.description: Attacks on Palestinians by Israeli extremists were rightly condemned, and Israel’s government must do more to stop it, but the media’s latest West Bank fixation risks feeding an anti-Israel pipeline.
item.content:encoded:
Let's call it what it was: masked settlers ambushing an NBC News crew and local Palestinians in the West Bank village of Jalud is an indefensible, unacceptable criminal act. This wasn't a "clash." It was an assault on journalists doing their jobs and people going about their daily lives.

Prime Minister Netanyahu condemned the attack, calling it a "criminal act of violence" committed by "a handful of rioters" who "harm Israel's standing in the world." Israeli security forces have confiscated three vehicles and opened an investigation — as Netanyahu called upon them to arrest those involved and deal with them to the full extent of the law. Sadly, this is not the first time, and Israel must show zero tolerance for such behavior by a lawless fringe — with arrests, prosecutions and prison sentences.

ISRAELI PRESIDENT HERZOG CALLS ANTISEMITISM A 'CONTAMINATION OF SOCIETIES' AS HATE CRIMES SURGE

But there's another important story here, and it's about the press itself. For over two years, Hamas and Gaza dominated nearly every broadcast, every U.N. session, every campus protest. That unparalleled coverage eclipsed the humanitarian crisis in Sudan, where the number of people in dire need of help is estimated at over 33 million (!) with close to 12 million people displaced from their homes.

However, even as the war in Gaza came to an end, global newsrooms didn't move on. They moved over. Judea and Samaria, also known as the West Bank, became the new venue of choice, the fresh well of footage and outrage needed to keep the anti-Israel narrative running at full volume. The war may be winding down. The narrative apparatus built around it is more active than ever.

JEWISH UCLA STUDENTS BEATEN WITH STICKS, PEPPER SPRAYED AND KNOCKED OUT BY ANTI-ISRAEL CAMPUS MOB: LAWSUIT

Acts of violence, such as the one in Jalud, are real and deserve coverage — but so does an enormous amount of violence elsewhere that never gets a fraction of this attention. Attacks on religious minorities across Africa, Asia and the Middle East routinely go unreported by the very same networks now camped out on the West Bank. Meanwhile, an isolated incident involving Israel — even one carried out by a small band of extremists the Israeli government itself condemns — has dominated the media for days.

The lesson audiences absorb, whether intended or not, is that violence only matters when Jews or Israel are on one side of it. That selective spotlight doesn't stay contained to foreign policy debates. It filters into U.N. resolutions, into government statements, into placards at protests and finally into open hostility toward Jews who have nothing to do with those acts at all.

SIGN UP FOR ANTISEMITISM EXPOSED NEWSLETTER

The pipeline runs from social media to the newsroom to the street with disturbing speed, and it demands the media’s accountability.

Lost in all of this is scale. The extremists carrying out these attacks are a minority of the minority, the very fringe among more than 500,000 Jewish residents living peacefully in Judea and Samaria, the biblical heartland of the Jewish State. The "unsettlers" was how U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee recently described them in an X post, "The ‘unsettlers’ betray the State of Israel, Judea/Samaria residents, civil law & the Torah."

The overwhelming majority are ordinary families: teachers, farmers, students, commuters who live under the daily threat of stabbings, shootings, and car-rammings that rarely make headlines anywhere. For example, only last week, a 16-year-old Palestinian jumped from behind and stabbed, moderately injuring a 24-year-old Israeli who stopped to shop near the village of Auja in the Jordan Valley. Where was this victim or his family interviewed? What coverage was given to the hateful education that propels a 16-year-old to viciously attack another person with a knife?!

The media's insistence on treating a fringe group as representative of that entire population — while ignoring the terror those same families face — isn't just lazy. It's a distortion that criminalizes an entire community and propels hatred and acts of violence on a global scale.

Antisemitism doesn't erupt in a vacuum. It needs a story, a grievance, a reason for outrage and there is no easier vehicle to manufacture one than the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Under the political charade, the ugliness under the cloak is clear: Israel is the Jew among the nations, and what is disguised as "political reporting" is really a biased attack on that Jew, the one and only Jewish state in the world.

When newsrooms chase Judea and Samaria the way they chased Gaza, amplifying the fringe, ignoring real terror and ignoring the peaceful majority, they aren't just shaping coverage, they're feeding the oldest hatred with the newest headlines.

No Jews, no news has ever been truer, or more dangerous.

item.title: Raging inferno erupts at Bali beachside restaurant party
item.description: Video shows flames engulfing a restaurant in Bali, Indonesia, after a reported balloon explosion during a birthday party sparked a massive inferno.
item.content:encoded:
A beachside party in Bali, Indonesia, erupted into chaos after a balloon reportedly exploded inside a popular restaurant, sparking a raging inferno.

Videos captured flames ripping through the Chez Gado-Gado restaurant in the Seminyak resort area during the incident Sunday, which left an Australian teenager hospitalized with burns, according to 7News.

"There was a 70th birthday, and they had two balloons on their table and a waitress went to light the candle on the birthday cake, but she lit it a bit too close to the balloon," Tara Borelli, a witness from Sydney, told News.com.au. "It popped, then exploded. We felt the heat from the pop."

"I just grabbed my daughter and little cousin and ran straight onto the beach towards the water," Borelli added, describing how the straw roof of the restaurant immediately caught fire and "within minutes" the entire restaurant was ablaze.

ONE TOURIST DEAD AFTER MASSIVE FIRE NEARLY DESTROYS CARIBBEAN RESORT; 1,690 EVACUATED

"It lit up like a firecracker... people were screaming and crying and running around," Paul Cole, another witness, told 9News.

The Badung Fire and Rescue Service said it took more than two hours to put out the flames and there were no casualties, according to The Bali Sun.

First Inspector I Gede Adi Saputra Jaya of the Denpasar Police, citing statements from witnesses at the scene, told reporters Monday that the fire is "strongly suspected" to have started after a balloon "was hit by a candle flame, causing it to explode and catch fire," the website added.

HUNDREDS OF POUNDS OF FIREWORKS EXPLODE, DESTROYING HOMES AND INJURING FIREFIGHTERS

"Initial extinguishing efforts using fire extinguishers by restaurant staff were unsuccessful because the fire had already grown large and spread quickly to the thatched roof," he reportedly said.

One witness told 9News, "There are the balloons, a lot of explosions, explosion and explosion and explosion, it was just, yeah, it was terrible."

"It was just bedlam," added Joe Xuereb, another witness. "As soon as the fire started, people didn’t know what to do."

The restaurant now says on its website that it is "temporarily closed."

item.title: Site where Jesus was crucified and buried reveals new evidence that backs biblical account
item.description: Ancient seeds and pollen beneath the Church of the Holy Sepulchre reveal a garden where Jesus Christ was crucified and bured, consistent with John 19:41 in the New Testament.
item.content:encoded:
Archaeologists have completed an excavation beneath one of Christianity's holiest sites, revealing a fuller picture of the ancient landscape where Jesus Christ was crucified and buried and providing support for scripture — something an early Christianity expert said he found very compelling. 

Francesca Stasolla, an archaeology professor at the Sapienza University of Rome, led the excavation in 2025, which focused on the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem.

The findings were recently published in Liber Annuus, the archaeological journal of Jerusalem's Studium Biblicum Franciscanum, in a 98-page preliminary report on the campaign.

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER MYSTERIOUS FACE HIDDEN FOR CENTURIES IN BOOK OF REVELATION CITY

The report follows findings noted by Fox News Digital last year.

At the time, Stasolla confirmed that her team had uncovered ancient seeds and pollen in layers dating between the site's use as a quarry and its later Roman occupation.

The evidence is consistent with John 19:41 in the New Testament: "Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid."

The pollen and seeds date to "between the use of the quarry and the Roman age, when the area had a funerary use," Stasolla told Fox News Digital in 2025.

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER MASSIVE ARTIFACT DEPICTING PHARAOH THOUGHT TO HAVE CHALLENGED MOSES IN EXODUS

"The quarry had to be gradually abandoned and as the stone extraction ended, it was used for agricultural areas and tombs," Stasolla said. 

"This must have been what it looked like in the first century A.D."

The church was identified as Jesus' burial place during the reign of Roman Emperor Constantine in the fourth century, when the first church was built there.

Though it has been a Christian pilgrimage site for nearly 1,700 years, archaeologists are now reconstructing what the area may have looked like around the time of Jesus.

LOST PAGES WITH 'GHOST' TEXT RECOVERED FROM ONE OF THE WORLD'S MOST IMPORTANT NEW TESTAMENT MANUSCRIPTS

Fox News Digital reached out to Stasolla for additional comment.

The findings add archaeological support to details described in the Gospel of John, said Douglas Estes, associate professor of religion at New College of Florida.

Estes, who specializes in early Christianity and was not involved in the research, told Fox News Digital that the Book of John is often dismissed by skeptics as exaggerated.

Archaeology has "over time, confirmed, again and again, details from the Gospel of John," he said — even though critics consider John's writings less accurate than the Gospels of Matthew, Mark and Luke.

He added, "For example, in the 19th century, scholars questioned whether or not there could be five colonnades [at the Pool of Bethesda in Jerusalem], as John 5 describes. Later archeological discoveries have found that, yes, there were five colonnades there."

He said that "in the same way, scholars have largely doubted whether or not Jesus would have been buried in an orchard.

"But instead we find confirmed that there was a garden there — and so the Gospel of John has been proven to be accurate again in the details."

item.title: China has found a new illicit drug market. America must shut it down
item.description: Chinese chemical manufacturers linked to fentanyl precursors are now shipping unapproved retatrutide peptides into U.S. homes via customs fraud.
item.content:encoded:
China has found another vulnerability in America’s borders and supply chain - and it's being exploited.

An illicit pipeline is bringing an experimental injectable drug from Chinese chemical manufacturers directly into American homes. The drug is retatrutide, commonly called "reta," and is in clinical trials as a potential treatment for obesity and type 2 diabetes. This means there is no FDA-approved version, no lawful generic and it’s illegal to sell to patients.

But the national security concern goes far beyond one drug.

JILLIAN MICHAELS EXPOSES DANGERS OF SELF-DOSING ILLEGAL 'GRAY MARKET' WEIGHT LOSS DRUGS

What we are witnessing is an illegal international supply chain that begins with chemical suppliers in Communist China, moves through customs fraud and concealed shipments, is relabeled by American middlemen and ends with an unapproved injectable drug in an American home.

We’ve seen this playbook before.

CLOSE THE BACKDOOR DRUG PIPELINE THAT’S EMBOLDENING ENEMIES AND HARMING THE PUBLIC

For years, Chinese chemical companies have supplied precursor chemicals used by cartels to make fentanyl. Now there is evidence that elements of this same infrastructure are being used for another lucrative American market: people looking for weight-loss drugs.

Blockchain researchers at Chainalysis were able to track proceeds from U.S. peptide sales flowing back to China-based chemical manufacturers that have produced synthetic opioids, such as fentanyl. TRM Labs has similarly detected a pattern of Chinese chemical companies that produce fentanyl precursors turning to the "peptide business."

EXPERT WARNS CHINA ALREADY WAGING ‘UNRESTRICTED WARFARE’ AGAINST US THROUGH FENTANYL, ESPIONAGE AND SABOTAGE

This should set off alarm bells across Washington.

The fentanyl crisis demonstrated what happens when foreign chemical suppliers, transnational criminal organizations and illicit financial networks exploit weaknesses in America’s borders and supply chains. We cannot make the same mistake twice by waiting until another illicit market becomes a full-blown crisis before confronting it.

FORMER TOP COP WARNS OF LOOPHOLE EXPLOITED BY ILLICIT CHINESE VAPE COMPANIES 'TARGETING OUR YOUTH'

The methods being used should also sound familiar.

Reta and other GLP-1 ingredients are being shipped to the United States under false descriptions that conceal what is actually inside the package and there is no reliable way for patients to verify the identity, purity, potency or sterility of what they are injecting into themselves. Once regulators have identified sellers engaged in this illegal behavior, the sellers then make changes needed to adapt.

‘WILD WEST’ PEPTIDE CRAZE SURGES BEYOND GLP-1S AS FDA FACES PRESSURE TO EASE ACCESS

Some vendors use coded names such as "GLP-3 RT." One vendor even distributed a "peptide cheat sheet" explaining that "GLP-3 RT" meant retatrutide and providing weekly dosing instructions. To further obscure their activity, sellers stamp packages "for research use only" while providing customers with dosing instructions, syringes and videos showing them how to prepare the drug for injection.

This is not simply skirting U.S. law. It is intentional evasion.

CBP OFFICERS SEIZE $67 MILLION IN ILLEGAL DRUGS AT SAN DIEGO BORDER PORTS, DHS SAYS

And it’s happening at scale.

In one operation, Customs and Border Protection officers in Cincinnati uncovered more than 300 master cartons from China containing roughly 5,000 individual peptide shipments. Reta was among the cache of chemicals seized.

CHINA, RUSSIA, IRAN AND NORTH KOREA FORM 'AXIS OF AGGRESSORS' THAT COULD OVERWHELM US, BOOK WARNS

This raises a larger question: if foreign chemical manufacturers can conceal thousands of unapproved injectable products in ordinary commerce and deliver them directly to Americans, what else can these networks move into the country?

That is why this must be treated as more than a pharmaceutical issue. This is a national security issue.

The immediate danger to consumers is also real. Products manufactured and distributed outside America’s safeguards leave buyers with no reliable way to know what they are injecting. There is no legitimate supply chain to inspect and no reliable mechanism to recall a dangerous batch.

President Donald Trump has correctly made securing our border and supply chains, fighting the illegal entry of drugs and confronting China’s economic aggression central priorities of his administration.

Now these principles must be applied to this emerging threat.

The Department of Homeland Security, Department of Justice, FDA, as well as state law enforcement should coordinate an aggressive enforcement strategy aimed at the entire network, from foreign manufacturers and deceptive importers to domestic distributors and the financial networks that profit from the trade.

Unlike many other policy challenges, the federal government already has many of the authorities it needs. What is missing is the muscular enforcement needed to combat the problem.

The private sector must also do its part. American tech companies, social giants, online platforms, payment processors and shipping companies cannot be idle bystanders while their platforms and services facilitate illicit commerce.

When sellers advertise unapproved injectable under coded names, provide dosing instructions and pay influencers a commission for each sale, it’s not difficult to understand what is happening.

If tech companies can identify copyrighted music, political content and alleged "misinformation" within seconds, then they should be able to identify an illegal injectable drug.

The lesson from the fentanyl crisis could not be clearer: America cannot afford to ignore foreign chemical supply chains until Americans begin to pay the price.

Today, the product is Reta. Tomorrow, it will be something else. The drug is the warning. The pipeline is the treat.

America must shut it down.

item.title: Explosion near German train station injures 2 Ukrainian citizens
item.description: Two Ukrainian citizens suffered minor injuries in the Augsburg train station explosion as police investigate a possible motive amid rising tensions.
item.content:encoded:
An explosion at a train station in Germany injured two people, both Ukrainian citizens, on Wednesday.

Police say they found a suspicious package following the explosion and ordered the Augsburg train station closed. The package was ultimately found to be harmless and trains began running again at 10 a.m. local time. The victims in the explosion were a 17-year-old girl and an 18-year-old man, neither of whom have been identified.

"We can give the all-clear — the object we found in front of the main train station was harmless, and we have reopened the station," police spokesperson Timo Küfner told The Associated Press. "The trains are running again, too."

The explosion occurred just after 3 a.m. local time and caused only minor injuries to the pair.

NATO MEMBER SCRAMBLES FIGHTER JETS AS RUSSIAN ATTACK ON UKRAINE KILLS 8

"It’s still too early to say anything about a possible motive for the overnight explosion, but we are investigating," said Küfner.

The incident comes just a day after Germany accused Russia of carrying out a failed drone sabotage operation at the Leipzig/Halle Airport.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Russia's consulate in Bonn will be closed and the contract for the Russian House cultural center in Berlin will be terminated after German authorities concluded Moscow was behind the Aug. 4 incident.

RUSSIA LINKED TO ARSON ATTACKS ON PROPERTIES CONNECTED TO UK PM KEIR STARMER, POLICE SAY

Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said forensic evidence and intelligence findings tied Russia to the attack, in which authorities found a drone carrying an explosive device beside a Ukrainian Antonov cargo aircraft at Leipzig/Halle Airport.

Officials said the device failed to explode because of a faulty detonator.

DRONE STRIKES APARTMENT BUILDING IN NATO MEMBER ROMANIA AS RUSSIA ATTACKS NEIGHBORING UKRAINE

Germany also said it believes a second drone collided with a nearby cargo aircraft, while officials have linked the incident to what Dobrindt described as Russia's "well-established pattern of Russian hybrid operations in Europe."

The Russian Embassy in Berlin called the accusation "absurd," while Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said Moscow would respond in a "mirror-image" fashion to Germany's actions. The embassy later described Berlin's measures as an "unprecedented escalation in Russian-German relations."

In addition to closing Russian diplomatic facilities, Wadephul announced tighter entry restrictions for Russian nationals and additional measures targeting Russia's shadow fleet. He also said he had summoned Russia's ambassador to Germany, Sergei Nechayev.

Fox News' Brittany Miller and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Prince William, Kate Middleton face 'Sussex circus' as Prince George prepares for Eton: expert
item.description: Prince George is set to start at Eton College, but the Sussexes' return to the U.K. has royal commentators warning of competing headlines and tension.
item.content:encoded:
While Prince William and Princess Kate's attention is focused on Prince George's approaching move to Eton, Prince Harry and Duchess Meghan's return to the U.K. could introduce a new source of family tension, according to royal experts.

George, 13, is expected to begin at Eton College this month, marking a major milestone for the Prince and Princess of Wales as their eldest child prepares to leave home for boarding school.

The occasion comes as Harry and Meghan have returned to the U.K. with their children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5. However, according to royal experts, the couple is expected to avoid making public comments or releasing photos that could overshadow George's first day.

PRINCE WILLIAM, KATE MIDDLETON COULD SEEK 'GENTLEMAN'S AGREEMENT' TO PROTECT PRINCE GEORGE AT ETON: EXPERTS

Still, royal commentator Kinsey Schofield told Fox News Digital that the Sussexes' presence could create an unpredictable wave of emotions for the Wales family during an already trying time.

"I have tremendous sympathy for the Prince and Princess of Wales," Schofield said. "Prince George is expected to start at Eton on September 8, which means this was their last Scottish summer holiday together before their teenage son leaves home for his first term at boarding school."

PRINCE WILLIAM, KATE MIDDLETON WRESTLED WITH MAJOR DECISION OVER PRINCE GEORGE'S FUTURE: EXPERT

"That is a huge emotional milestone for any family, and instead of being able to quietly enjoy that time together, Harry and Meghan have brought the circus back to town," she added.

Schofield said William and Kate may be forced to navigate the media attention surrounding Harry and Meghan while trying to maintain privacy for their children.

PRINCE WILLIAM ‘BLINDSIDED’ BY HARRY, MEGHAN RETURN AS KATE FEARS NEW TURMOIL FROM ROYAL FEUD: EXPERTS

"What I think will be particularly difficult for William and Catherine is the unpredictability," Schofield said. "Harry and Meghan have a history of making their own plans, generating enormous media attention and operating outside the traditional royal structure."

"Now William and Catherine are sending their eldest child away from home for the first time while simultaneously having to navigate the Sussexes' return and all of the uncertainty surrounding it," she added.

PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE'S UK RETURN SIGNALS ‘SPECTACULAR DEFEAT’ AS ROYAL EXPERTS WARN OF WILLIAM SHOWDOWN

Schofield said George should be allowed to begin his new chapter without being pulled into the ongoing media frenzy surrounding his family.

"George deserves to begin this new chapter of his life without being dragged into another cycle of speculation about his uncle and aunt," Schofield said.

PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE ARRIVE IN UK WITH KIDS, MARKING DRAMATIC RETURN 6 YEARS AFTER ROYAL EXIT

Richard Fitzwilliams, a royal commentator, said the Sussexes' return could intensify the pressure on the royal family and the Palace.

PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE’S UK MOVE PUTS FRESH SPOTLIGHT ON THEIR EXPLOSIVE CLAIMS AGAINST ROYAL FAMILY

"The people would love them to depart, though the circus they create is weird and anthropologically fascinating," he said.

The reported agreement for Harry and Meghan to "lay low" during George's Eton debut was previously described by royal broadcaster Neil Sean as an effort to prevent the Sussexes from overshadowing the future king's historic first day.

"The Sussexes have assured the king that they will not hijack or derail major royal events, notably the first day of school term for Prince George at Eton," Sean previously told Fox News Digital. "By that, no pictures or comment from either one on that day in September."

"The Palace is incredibly protective of that narrative, and any competing headline — especially one involving Harry and Meghan — threatens to distract from the 'steady, future-focused' brand the Prince and Princess of Wales have worked so hard to build."

Matta added that it would "certainly be a shame for his first days at Eton to see him embroiled in a 'feud' narrative with his uncle and aunt."

Harry and Meghan stepped down as senior working royals in 2020 and later moved to California. They are expected to retain ties to California while re-establishing themselves in Britain.

Schofield described the couple's reported U.K. plans as "a trial run rather than a definitive homecoming."

British broadcaster Helena Chard told Fox News Digital that Harry and Meghan are "keeping their options open."

item.title: New weight-loss compound melts fat without curbing appetite — and preserves muscle
item.description: University of California, Berkeley scientists found TOFA boosted energy expenditure in obese mice without the lean muscle loss tied to semaglutide.
item.content:encoded:
A team of researchers led by scientists at the University of California, Berkeley, has identified a decades-old oral compound that produced substantial weight loss in obese mice.

Rather than suppressing appetite, the compound appears to boost energy expenditure, according to a study published in Science Advances.

The molecule, known as TOFA, reduced the mice’s body weight by an average of 18% without changing how much they ate or causing a statistically significant loss of lean mass.

NEW OBESITY TREATMENT MAY HELP PRESERVE MUSCLE DURING WEIGHT LOSS

While popular injectable weight-loss medications such as semaglutide can produce substantial weight loss partly by reducing food intake, some patients experience gastrointestinal side effects and loss of lean mass.

Studies have also found that people often regain a significant amount of weight after stopping treatment.

Preserving muscle during weight loss remains one of the greatest clinical hurdles in obesity medicine, according to experts.

"Muscle mass is really important for our function during the day. It helps fight the effects of aging," Dr. Leslie Pristas, a bariatric surgeon and owner of Best Life Bariatrics and Medical Weight Loss in Northeast Ohio, told Fox News Digital.

"Building muscle is really hard. It takes a really long time. So if we can avoid having muscle loss while we're having weight loss, that's going to be so much better."

THIS COULD BE WHY YOUR WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATION ISN’T DELIVERING RESULTS

Instead of primarily targeting appetite, TOFA acts inside cells, according to the researchers. It blocks enzymes involved in the production of lipids, including fats such as triglycerides, while also activating cellular receptors that turn on genes involved in fat burning and energy production.

Treated mice burned up to 18% more energy under room-temperature and mildly warm conditions, without becoming less active or developing a dangerous increase in body temperature.

When the researchers combined TOFA with existing obesity drugs such as semaglutide or tirzepatide, the combination treatments produced greater reductions in body weight and improvements in blood sugar, insulin and triglyceride levels than either drug alone.

Mice treated with TOFA maintained body weights close to control levels after treatment ended, while mice previously given semaglutide began rapidly regaining weight.

PATIENTS TAKING WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS OFTEN MAKE 5 CRITICAL MISTAKES, DOCTOR WARNS

Pristas urged caution against assuming that any single medication could permanently prevent post-treatment weight gain.

"Obesity is super complex," she said. "There's not just one mechanism by which everyone gains weight or even a single person gains weight. There are a lot of overlapping factors."

"Once we have extra weight on our body, that kind of becomes where our body thinks we're supposed to be. That becomes our body's weight set point," she noted, adding that if someone stops a medication abruptly, the body may then work to return to its previous weight.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The compound also showed promise in mouse models for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), a form of fatty liver disease. Mice given TOFA had less liver fat, inflammation and fibrosis (scarring).

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

TOFA achieved these liver benefits without increasing triglyceride levels in the blood, the researchers noted. Some similar metabolic drugs have caused triglycerides to rise, creating potential cardiovascular and other health concerns that have complicated their development.

The authors emphasized that all the animal experiments involved male mice. Future studies will need to determine whether TOFA produces similar results in female animals.

The drug has not yet been tested in people, so researchers still don't know what dose would be appropriate, whether it is safe to use over long periods, or whether it could cause subtle toxicities or other safety problems.

Pristas emphasized that early mouse data must be weighed carefully against potential hidden side effects in humans.

"If it sounds too good to be true, it's probably too good to be true," she said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"When you're talking about manipulating our bodies' manufacturing or processing of lipids, it's complex. And so there can be downstream effects that we don't want. That's where we can't get too excited."

However, the expert said the treatment could eventually benefit people, either on its own or in combination with another therapy.

The study authors disclosed that several researchers are co-founders, officers or equity holders in ReRx Therapeutics, a company with an agreement giving it the option to develop UC Berkeley’s TOFA-related discovery.

item.title: Nation’s largest teachers union under fire as controversial agenda puts century-old federal charter at risk
item.description: Sen. Bill Cassidy's report targets the NEA's ties to the Zinn Education Project and Rethinking Schools over curriculum glorifying political violence.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE — The head of an influential Senate committee is urging Congress to reconsider the charter of the nation’s largest teachers union, citing its far-left associations and allegedly irresponsible financial activity.

In recent years, the National Education Association, which represents roughly 3 million educators, has come under fire for mobilizing students and teachers to support liberal activist campaigns, been criticized by its Jewish members for failing to address antisemitism, spent millions in membership dues supporting left-wing causes and partnered with organizations that portray political violence and far-left extremism favorably.

Now, Sen. Bill Cassidy, the Republican chair of the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions, is calling on his colleagues to take a closer look at the NEA’s congressional charter.

BLISTERING REPORT EXPOSES HOW NATIONAL K-12 GROUP'S DEI AGENDA IS TRICKLING DOWN TO LOCAL SCHOOLS

"Children are struggling to read and to do basic math. Instead of helping students succeed, teachers’ unions are injecting a dangerous, anti-American agenda into our classrooms," Cassidy told Fox News Digital. "Parents deserve to send their children to school without worrying that they will be indoctrinated with DEI and taught that Americans have ‘misplaced faith’ in our institutions."

Cassidy, in a report outlining the NEA’s activity obtained exclusively by Fox News Digital, puts a spotlight on the Zinn Education Project and Rethinking Schools — a pair of interlinked educational nonprofits that the top teachers union has collaborated with extensively.

EXCLUSIVE: SPLC'S 'FAR-LEFT' 'ANTI-RACISM' CURRICULUM FOUND IN CLASSROOMS AS EARLY AS KINDERGARTEN: WATCHDOG

The Zinn Education Project and Rethinking Schools, for instance, have published curricular materials that justify the actions of the Black Panther Party — a left-wing militant Black nationalist organization that operated during the Cold War — and praise its members, including those who were involved in acts of political violence, according to the report. 

"The Marxist and communist ideologies espoused by the Black Panther Party are inconsistent and incompatible with the foundation of the United States Constitution," Cassidy’s report, published by the HELP committee, reads. "The Black Panthers advocated for the use of armed force against police and were involved in the murders of civil servants and members of their own party."

SCOPE OF SPLC'S DEEPLY EMBEDDED INFLUENCE TRAINING TEACHERS NATIONWIDE UNCOVERED IN SWEEPING REPORT

Rethinking Schools also published a lesson plan where students are meant to role-play as "queer liberation" activists fighting against the "Religious Right," according to the report. Another lesson plan, titled "Expanding Intersectional Queer History in the Elementary Grades," instructs teachers on how to incorporate LGBTQ material into lessons for young students.

The union has worked closely with the duo of nonprofits over the years, giving them prominent space and speaking opportunities at conferences, collaborating with them on curriculum development and nationwide teaching events, and praising and promoting their lessons. The union has also incorporated the groups’ work into educator handbooks and helped distribute their lesson plans to teachers.

HOUSE GOP LAUNCHES PROBE INTO 5 MAJOR LABOR UNIONS OVER DEM SPENDING DESPITE MAGA MEMBERSHIP BASE

Congress chartered the NEA in 1906 under the expectation that it would "elevate the character and advance the interests of the profession of teaching; and to promote the cause of education in the United States," a mission Cassidy and some other Republicans argue it has since strayed from. Revoking the NEA’s charter would primarily be a reputational blow to the union, as it would still be able to operate even without it.

As another example of the NEA allegedly failing to live up to its charter, the HELP committee points to its involvement in the left-wing protest movements.

MAY DAY PROTESTS ‘JUST THE BEGINNING’ OF STUDENT ACTIVISM PUSH, EXPERT WARNS

The labor union promoted and participated in the 2026 May Day protests, which were critical of President Donald Trump and his Republican allies. In one planning webinar the NEA hosted in the lead-up to the demonstrations, educators were advised to "bring activism into the classroom," targeting children as young as three years old. Students in Chicago were reportedly encouraged by teachers to skip class for the protests, even as Chicago Public Schools see subpar reading and math competency scores.

On the financial side of things, Cassidy points to data showing that, since 2015, the NEA has contributed hundreds of millions of dollars to advocacy organizations and political action committees, the vast majority of which are left-of-center. In some cases, political organizations funded by the NEA later provided members of the union’s leadership team with cushy jobs, according to the report.

FAR-LEFT ACTIVIST CONFERENCE AT TEACHERS UNION HQ RAISES CLASSROOM CONCERNS

"The central issue is not whether every such expenditure is impermissible. Rather, it is whether members receive sufficient transparency about how their dues are used, whether union leadership has adopted adequate safeguards against conflicts of interest and whether these expenditures advance the purposes for which members joined the union in the first place," the Senate committee report reads.

Organizations funded by the NEA include the Sixteen Thirty Fund and the Tides Foundation, two of the largest Democratic-aligned dark money operations in the country, as well as millions to its own PAC, which almost exclusively supports Democratic candidates.

JEWISH EDUCATORS FACE RAMPANT ANTISEMITISM IN TEACHERS UNIONS, NEW REPORT FINDS

The HELP committee report also alleges that the NEA has failed to represent the interests of Jewish educators, citing an August 2025 letter where the union’s Jewish Affairs Caucus claimed its members reported "shunning, harassment and antisemitic comments" at the union’s annual assembly.

While not congressionally chartered like the NEA, the American Federation of Teachers drew flak from Cassidy’s report for many of the same reasons.

The report cites the AFT’s participation in "No Kings" protests against President Donald Trump, its boycott of Target over immigration enforcement and its advocacy on LGBTQ+ issues, as well as its routing of tens of millions of dollars to liberal causes, as evidence of alleged mission drift at the union.

The NEA, AFT, Rethinking Schools and the Zinn Education Project did not respond to requests for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Tuesday.

The scrutiny comes as the NEA transitions to new leadership. Princess R. Moss, a former NEA vice president and secretary-treasurer, began a three-year term as president on Tuesday, succeeding Becky Pringle, who led the union for six years.

item.title: DeSantis endorses Florida GOP slate including Byron Donalds in governor's race
item.description: Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis endorsed a "slate" of candidates that included GOP gubernatorial candidate Rep. Byron Donalds.
item.content:encoded:
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis endorsed a "slate" of Republicans statewide Tuesday, including GOP gubernatorial nominee U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds. 

"I'm endorsing the slate here tonight ... because I know it's important for the state of Florida," DeSantis said at the Florida GOP Leadership Forum in Tampa.

The event showcased Donalds, Attorney General James Uthmeier, Florida Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia and Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson.

Last year, DeSantis appointed Ingoglia as CFO and Uthmeier as attorney general. Later in 2025, the governor endorsed Ingoglia for election to the CFO post. He then backed Simpson for re-election this year. 

TRUMP'S HANDPICKED DESANTIS SUCCESSOR WINS CROWDED GOP PRIMARY FOR FLORIDA GOVERNOR

"Tonight I was honored to earn Governor @RonDeSantis’s endorsement," Donalds wrote in a post on X.

"Governor DeSantis has done incredible work to make Florida the envy of America. As your next Governor, I will build on his success and defend the Florida Dream," he said.

FORMER FLORIDA GOVERNOR HOPEFUL HAULED OUT OF COUNTY MEETING AFTER PROTESTING ISRAEL INVESTMENTS

Donalds, who won the Florida GOP gubernatorial primary in August with the backing of President Donald Trump, will face Democratic gubernatorial candidate former U.S. Rep. David Jolly in the general election.

While he is currently running for governor as a Democrat, Jolly previously served in the U.S. House of Representatives as a Republican.

BYRON DONALDS SHUTS DOWN BILL MAHER'S CLAIM ON GOP PRIMARY RACISM, SAYS 'FLORIDA IS A MERITOCRACY'

Under the Florida Constitution, DeSantis, who is serving his second consecutive term, is not eligible to seek another consecutive term as governor this year.

"No person who has, or but for resignation would have, served as governor or acting governor for more than six years in two consecutive terms shall be elected governor for the succeeding term," the Florida Constitution states.

item.title: Costco's famous $1.50 hot dog combo gets simple swap that can slash your sugar intake
item.description: A registered dietitian weighs in on Costco's new bottled water option for its iconic hot dog combo, revealing how much sugar the soda swap saves.
item.content:encoded:
Months after Costco began allowing customers to swap the soda in its iconic $1.50 hot dog combo for bottled water, shoppers are still debating what constitutes the best value at the warehouse club's food court.

A recent Reddit discussion about Costco's food court pricing began with a shopper questioning the logic of buying a soda alone for 79 cents when another 71 cents would get customers a hot dog, too.

The conversation soon flipped the question around, with customers wanting the hot dog but not necessarily the soda.

COSTCO SPARKS BAGEL BACKLASH AMONG CUSTOMERS AS DOWNSIZED PACKS IGNITE PRICING DEBATE

"I want the hot dog," one commenter wrote. "The soda is a byproduct."

Another commenter mentioned sometimes buying multiple hot dogs but only wanting one drink, adding, "Good thing now you can get the bottled water instead of the soda."

Costco earlier this year began offering shoppers at participating locations the option to substitute a 16.9-ounce bottle of Kirkland Signature water for the 20-ounce fountain drink that traditionally accompanies its $1.50 hot dog combo. The soda option, which includes free refills, remains available.

The choice raises a question for customers trying to balance nutrition with the value of Costco's famously inexpensive meal: How much healthier is the combo if shoppers choose water?

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Lauren Manaker, a registered dietitian based in Charleston, South Carolina, told Fox News Digital that switching to water can cut a meaningful amount of sugar from the meal, although the swap alone does not necessarily make the Costco staple healthy.

"I don't know if it makes a world of a difference because a hot dog is not what I would consider to be the healthiest choice out there," Manaker said.

"I will say that it can offer significant savings in terms of sugar intake. So, if that's a concern for people, that can be a positive change."

For the occasional Costco food court customer, however, Manaker said the choice between the two beverages is unlikely to be particularly consequential.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"Whether you choose water or soda, I don't think it's going to have a profound impact on your overall health," she said.

There is also the question of value. A fountain soda with free refills may appear to offer more for the same $1.50 price, but Manaker noted that bottled water has its own appeal.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"I don't love the taste of the tap water and bottled water can be pricey," she said.

Either way, Costco's price tag remains untouched: hot dog, drink and all, is still $1.50.

The first was held in June and was described by Page Six Hollywood as a "glitzy Dem fundraiser" at the home of Hollywood producer Peter Chernin. Fox News Digital reached out to the Lindelofs and Chernin for comment.

Meanwhile, Talarico’s opponent, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, will gather in Dallas for the Republican National Committee’s midterm convention, along with President Donald Trump and other Republicans. The same night Republicans rally in Dallas, former President Barack Obama will headline a Democratic House fundraiser in New York, according to The New York Times. The events put prominent Democrats on the coasts while Republicans gather in Texas.

Fox News Digital previously reported that donors from outside Texas accounted for roughly 50% of the funds raised by Talarico, according to first-quarter campaign finance records.

TALARICO SAYS THE DIVIDE IS 'TOP VS. BOTTOM' — THEN HEADS TO ONE OF AMERICA'S RICHEST DONOR ENCLAVES

Talarico is taking heat from Republicans for his out-of-state fundraising. RNC spokesperson Zach Kraft told Fox News Digital that "it is no surprise that James Talarico feels more comfortable in crazy liberal California than when his handlers force him to wear a fake cowboy hat and rent a pickup truck to pretend to be a 'real' Texan."

Fox News Digital reached out to Talarico’s campaign for comment but did not receive a response by the time of publication.

Talarico currently serves as a progressive Democratic lawmaker in the Texas House of Representatives. Since winning the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate, Republicans have continually knocked him for his record of controversial statements, including calling God "nonbinary," saying that there are six sexes and saying that reducing meat consumption was "existential" to fight climate change.

JAMES TALARICO DOESN'T DRIVE HIS OWN TRUCK IN VIRAL TEXAS CAMPAIGN AD FEATURING DODGE RAM

Despite the attacks, Talarico and Paxton are running a tight race, and many Democrats believe this could be the year Texas finally flips blue. A Fox News poll from July gave Talarico a 3-point edge over Paxton, 51% to 48%, which was within the survey’s margin of sampling error.

Paxton, meanwhile, has told Fox News Digital that Talarico’s lead is not surprising given his head start in the general election following his particularly messy primary runoff against incumbent Sen. John Cornyn.

Speaking with Fox News on Sunday, Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., said that "money is an issue" in the race.

FIRST ON FOX: MAJOR CORNYN BACKER GOES ALL-IN FOR PAXTON AS GOP RALLIES AFTER RED STATE SHOCK POLL

"Mr. Talarico has been raising bucketloads of money from California, Hollywood," he said.

He called on Trump to help Paxton with cash, saying, "We in the Senate don’t have the money budgeted for Texas; we need help from the president."
